ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: If the buffalo population increased, what would happen to the grass population?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: There are two food chains in the image. Part A is labeled "Great Plains food chain for Native Americans", showing "Perennial grass" pointing by an arrow to "Buffalo", and then "Buffalo" pointing by an arrow to "Humans". Part B shows "Annual Crop" pointing to "Humans". The question asks what will happen to the amount of grass if the number of buffalo increases. According to the food chain in Part A, the arrow points from perennial grass to buffalo, indicating that buffalo eat grass. Therefore, an increase in the number of buffalo will cause more grass to be eaten, so the amount of grass will decrease.
